title: A 48-Metal Cluster Exhibiting a Large Magnetocaloric Effect

synthesis.procedure: Ni(CH3COO)2·6H2O (0.249 g, 1.0 mmol) and Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.902 g, 2.0 mmol) were added to deionized water (5 mL) and anhydrous ethanol (15 mL). The solution was heated to about 70 °C. Freshly prepared aqueous NaOH (1.0 M) was added dropwise with stirring to pH 5–6, followed by NaCl (10 mg). More NaOH solution was added to incipient permanent precipitation at approximately pH 6–6.5. The mixture was refluxed for 2 h and filtered; evaporation of the filtrate under ambient conditions gave grassy block-shaped crystals over two weeks.

reagents.name: sodium hydroxide, freshly prepared aqueous solution

synthesis.time: 2 h at reflux; crystals obtained over two weeks
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered after reflux; filtrate evaporated under ambient conditions to give grassy block-shaped crystals.

properties.summary: The susceptibility decreases markedly on cooling, consistent with antiferromagnetic interactions and possible zero-field splitting. Field-dependent magnetization gives a large low-temperature magnetocaloric effect.

measurements.name: Curie–Weiss temperature θ
measurements.conditions: Fit to susceptibility data from 2 to 300 K

measurements.name: magnetic entropy change −ΔSm
measurements.conditions: 3 K; field change ΔH = 7 T; calculated from magnetization data

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The tubular 48-metal core is described as a sandwich: two outer 18-metal Gd12Ni6 wheels assembled from vertex-sharing Gd3Ni cubane-like units enclose a 24-metal Gd24 wheel assembled from square-pyramidal Gd5 units. Sharing Gd atoms between the wheels joins these components into the tube.
